title: Singers with the band: Joya Sherrill, Kay Davis, Betty Roche
summary: Greer lists women vocalists after Ivie, and Come Sunday from Black, Brown and Beige.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: we played there, a whole different program written. One segment -- half a segment was written, new composition that he would start a concert. But like -- what's this thing?..... Some guy asked, I think Brooksie played a solo last night, -- what did you ask me?
You played a piece on "Come Sunday" or --

"Come Sunday," yeah. Because they had -- we had three girls singing in our band, Joya Sherrill --- quit then -- Ivie had in, Joya Sherrill, Marie Ellington, who later married Nat King Cole and Kay Davis, little girl who married a big lawyer in Chicago. She sang all them high notes. So they --
Betty Roche for a little while, too, didn't you?
Yeah, Betty joined us after Ivie got so sick she couldn't travel no more. She joined us. But Betty Roche never sang "Black Brown and Beige," you know.
Yes, she sang, "The blues ain't nothing but something." Yeah, Betty sang. Sang good, too. Oooee. Roche, she was something else.
